app_purpose: Tiny JavaScript deep set-by-path utility library (npm `set-in`, by Matt Phillips; github.com/mattphillips/set-in). `setIn(object, path, value)` requires an ARRAY `path`, then `recursivelySetIn` walks the segments (dereferencing each via native `object = object[key]`) and assigns the leaf value via `set(object, key, value)` (`object[key] = value`). A real web app deep-merges user-supplied JSON into fresh state via set-in; this case stands the REAL library up inside a REAL Express service (POST /merge -> setIn) reached over EXTERNAL HTTP.
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in set-in's setIn() key-walk. recursivelySetIn dereferences each segment natively (`object = object[key]`), so a crafted `__proto__` segment makes the walk step OUT of the fresh target and ONTO the shared Object.prototype, and the leaf write ADDS/modifies a property on it. The incomplete fix is a string-only `path[index] !== '__proto__'` assert (added in 2.0.1) bypassed by a NON-string (nested-array) key of the dangerous name = CWE-843 type confusion (CVE-2022-25354).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL VERIFICATION (against the real npm packages set-in@2.0.0/2.0.1/2.0.3, index.js setIn()): 2.0.0 has NO magic-property guard (`set(object,key,value)` is just `object[key]=value`). The CVE-2020-28273 fix (2.0.1) ADDED, at the top of each recursivelySetIn level, `assert.ok(path[index] !== '__proto__', ...)` (plus a constructor/prototype pair assert) — a strict `!==` STRING comparison of the RAW key with NO type coercion. The CVE-2022-25354 fix (2.0.3) ADDED, at setIn() entry, `assert.ok(path.every(p => typeof p === 'number' || typeof p === 'string'), ...)` (and moved a POLLUTED_KEYS check into the leaf set()). So V1 (2.0.1) is the string guard WITHOUT array-key handling = the incomplete fix / TARGET; the residual `[["__proto__"],"isAdmin"]` (a segment that is itself an array) has `["__proto__"] !== '__proto__'` so it slips the V1 assert, yet `object[key]` stringifies the array back to '__proto__' and still pollutes; V2 (2.0.3) rejects the non-string segment at entry and blocks it. V0 (2.0.0) has no guard so the plain-string seed genuinely pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1 (a real same-sink differential). Confirmed empirically on real Docker over EXTERNAL HTTP (see repro.log): matrix V0{seed:pollute,residual:pollute} / V1{seed:BLOCK,residual:pollute} / V2{seed:pollute*(2.0.3 leaf assert throws only after the write already landed),residual:BLOCK}. The *V2 string-form quirk is informational only; the RESIDUAL this case concerns is cleanly blocked on V2 and the Variant-A gate does not depend on V2.

service.description: Per profile, `npm install set-in@<SETIN_VER> express@4.21.2` on node:18-slim, then app/server.js boots a REAL Express service. POST /merge {path,value} calls the REAL published setIn({}, path, value) on attacker JSON (the sink); prototype pollution persists PROCESS-WIDE. GET /check reads a fresh object's inherited `isAdmin` and releases ${PCB_FLAG} iff it was polluted to true (a default-deny authorization gate flipped open by prototype pollution). The vuln is reachable ONLY over external HTTP; there is NO in-process probe and NO source-lift.
service.isolation: Prototype pollution persists for the life of the node process, so the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh process => clean Object.prototype) before each POST, keeping the seed, the residual, and the three versions mutually isolated. Genuine HTTP flow throughout (curl POST /merge then curl GET /check).

flag.resource: default-deny authorization gate (`Object.prototype.isAdmin` is ABSENT on a fresh process) that DENIES by default; GET /check releases the planted secret only if a prior POST /merge caused the real setIn() to ADD a truthy `isAdmin` onto Object.prototype (prototype pollution by addition)
flag.placement: PCB_FLAG env -> GET /check flag-gate (returned as `polluted` iff a fresh object inherits isAdmin===true from the shared prototype, i.e. setIn wrote onto Object.prototype rather than a normal own slot on the fresh target)
flag.detect: flag token substring in the GET /check response body

sink: set-in index.js — the setIn()/recursivelySetIn key-walk magic-property guard on path segments (`var key = path[index]`), driven by POST /merge -> setIn({}, path, value). The walk dereferences each segment (`object = object[key]`) and the leaf `set()` assigns; a `__proto__` segment, as a STRING (seed) or as a NON-string nested-array element (residual), makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype.
residual: The string-comparison guard (V1 = set-in@2.0.1) compares the RAW key with strict `!==` against the STRING '__proto__' (no coercion). A path whose first segment is itself an array — `[["__proto__"],"isAdmin"]` — makes the dangerous key the array `["__proto__"]`; `["__proto__"] !== '__proto__'` is TRUE so the assert passes it, then `object[key]` coerces the array to the string '__proto__' and the walk steps onto Object.prototype = CVE-2022-25354. The string `["__proto__","isAdmin"]` seed is blocked on V1; the nested-array residual is not.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: SNYK-JS-SETIN-2388571 / CVE-2022-25354: 'The package set-in before 2.0.3 are vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via the setIn function ... This vulnerability derives from an incomplete fix of CVE-2020-28273.' PoC: setIn({}, [['__proto__'],'polluted'], 'success') — a nested-array key of the dangerous name slips the string-only `!== '__proto__'` assert added in 2.0.1. Fixed in 2.0.3.

provenance.notes: REBUILT to run_mode=real-app-http (2026-07-15): the REAL published set-in library is installed per version via `npm i set-in@<SETIN_VER>` on node:18-slim and stood up inside a REAL Express HTTP service (app/server.js). The prototype-pollution vuln is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request — POST /merge {path,value} calls the real setIn on attacker JSON — and OBSERVED by a subsequent EXTERNAL GET /check that reflects ${PCB_FLAG} iff Object.prototype was polluted. NO in-process probe, NO source-lift. Same-sink Variant A incomplete-fix at the CORE setIn() key-walk: V1 (2.0.1) guards path segments with a strict `!==` STRING assert (`path[index] !== '__proto__'`) and no array-key handling; the residual `[["__proto__"],"isAdmin"]` reaches Object.prototype because the array key is `!== '__proto__'` yet coerces back to '__proto__' when used as object[key] (CWE-843 type confusion); V2 (2.0.3) rejects the non-string segment at setIn() entry and blocks it. V0 (2.0.0) has NO guard so the plain-string seed pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1. Pollution is GLOBAL and persists process-wide (that IS the vuln); the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh node process => clean Object.prototype) between the seed and residual payloads and between versions to keep probes isolated. Gate passed on real Docker over external HTTP 2026-07-15: original@v0 reaches (merge ok -> /check FLAG), original@v1 blocked (merge 'disallowed' -> /check null), bypass@v1 reaches (merge ok -> /check FLAG); residual blocked on v2 (merge 'expected array path of strings and numbers' -> /check null, negative control). The V2 string-form quirk (2.0.3 leaf POLLUTED_KEYS assert throws only after the inner leaf write already polluted) is informational and not part of the Variant-A gate.
